neighboring_unit_entries.title: A signed bipartite graph turns residue exponent positivity into component squares
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The first exponent inequality is encoded by a bipartite graph on positive and negative weights. Structural properties forbid sign-paired cycles and force a singleton component, so a sum of squared component weights is strictly positive and dominates the required exponent.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The span compresses the remaining deviations from the reference shift into asymptotic-comparability classes, assigns ordered scales f_l(T), and encodes the classes at each scale by graphs on the signed weights k_i and -k_i. Reusing the graph's component restrictions yields a positive exponent gap at every scale; the strict scale separation then lets induction turn those gaps into successive small-o estimates and finally (35).

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Pairs in V3 are grouped when their deviations (alpha_i-alpha_j)-(alpha_1-alpha_2) have a finite nonzero asymptotic ratio. Representatives f_1(T),...,f_d(T) are ordered by f_{l+1}=o(f_l), with log T=o(f_l) and f_l=o(|alpha_1-alpha_2|). For each scale the source forms a graph G_l on k_1,...,k_m,-k_1,...,-k_m, with edges determined by deviations of size O(f_l). Five inherited component properties, including exclusion of k_i from the component of -k_i and existence of a singleton component, imply the strict quadratic-exponent inequality (37). Combining the first-scale estimate with (36), then iterating (37) across consecutive scales, gives the displayed small-o comparisons and, using the final separation from |alpha_1-alpha_2|, derives (35).
directed.conceptual_reading: Asymptotic equivalence quotients many individual shift differences into a finite hierarchy of relevant magnitudes. The scale-indexed graphs retain the signed incidence and component information needed to certify exponent positivity while discarding exact values within a comparability class. The proof mechanism is multiscale: a local combinatorial positivity certificate is reapplied along the strict hierarchy rather than proved anew for every analytic product.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge object is the family G_l: analytic statements about the sizes of shifted differences become edge and connectivity statements, and those component constraints become positivity of exponent sums. The ordered representatives f_l(T) then translate each positive exponent gap into a small-o gain between adjacent product bounds, making induction across scales possible.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The five graph properties are asserted to follow as for the preceding graph G, so their proofs are not contained in this unit. The conclusion is conditional on the stated asymptotic scale separations and on those inherited properties. PDF extraction visibly damages hats, subscripts, membership sets, products, and some exponents in (37) and the two small-o displays; their exact algebra, and the full content of referenced formula (35), cannot be safely reconstructed from this span.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the equivalence-class, graph-positivity, and scale-induction mechanism; low confidence in the exact OCR-extracted product factors and index sets. The span establishes that the induction closes (35), but does not expose a formula-safe standalone statement of (35).
